records.section: a b s t r a c t

records.text: The hot deformation behavior of low-density high-strength FeeMneAleC steel at T 900 $- 1 1 5 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ and $\dot { \varepsilon } = 0 . 0 1 \mathrm { - } 1 0 { \ s } ^ { - 1 }$ is studied using the Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator. The rheological stress curve characteristics of the steel are analyzed through experimental data and the dynamic recrystallization activation energy is calculated. The critical strain/stress, peak strain/stress and steady-state strain/stress models of dynamic recrystallization are characterized by introducing the dimensionless parameter Zener-Hollomon. The microstructure evolution is analyzed and the dynamic recrystallization state diagram of the steel is drawn. The results indicated that the steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and a positive strain rate-sensitive material. The dynamic recrystallization activation energy is 669.844 kJ mol<sup>1</sup>. With the decrease of <sup>ε</sup>\_ or the increase of T, the Z parameter decreases gradually and the dynamic recrystallization behavior is more likely to occur; however, its grain size increases accordingly. The fine and uniform grain structure can be obtained by hot working in the range of $9 5 0 - 1 0 0 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } / 0 . 0 1 - 0 . 1 \ : s ^ { - 1 }$ <sup>1</sup> and 1050 e1100 $^ { \circ } { \bf C } / 1 { - } 1 0 \ { \bf s } ^ { - 1 }$ . Finally, the prediction model for the dynamic recrystallization average grain size is established, and the correlation coefficient (R) of the prediction model is 0.996; therefore, the model has a high prediction accuracy.

records.text: Introduction
records.section: Introduction

records.text: With the rapid development of the automobile industry, automotive lightweight materials have become an important research topic. Among them, FeeMneAleC steel has good corrosion resistance, low density and excellent comprehensive mechanical properties, having great application prospect in the fields of weight reduction, collision safety and the complex working conditions of the automobiles structure [1e4]. In addition, thermoplastic deformation can effectively refine the grain size and improve the properties of forgings and microstructure. In the field of actual production, the microstructure is primarily controlled by way of thermal machining. Dynamic recrystallization (DRX) is beneficial to grain refinement and homogenization and is an important deformation mechanism to improve the microstructure and properties within the hot working process [5e7]. Therefore, in-depth studies on the microstructure evolution and DRX behavior of FeeMneAleC steel are of great significance for the formulation and optimization of the hot forging process of the steel.
records.section: Introduction

records.text: At present, reports on FeeMneAleC steel primarily focus on smelting, heat treatment and mechanical properties. For example, Moon et al. [8] studied Fee30Mn-10.5Al-1.1C-(0e5) Mo steel. It was found that Mo-enriched $\mathtt { M } _ { 6 } \mathtt { C }$ and ${ \bf M } _ { 2 3 } { \bf C } _ { 6 }$ carbides precipitate during the solution treatment when the Mo content is higher than 4%, inhibiting the growth of the austenite grains during the solution treatment. Liu et al. [9] heated Fee11Mne10Al-1.25C steel and cooled the steel via three different methods. It was found that the distribution of -carbide in the samples after intense cooling was more uniform than that of the samples after air and water cooling; this, the corresponding mechanical properties were superior. However, the research reports on the hot deformation behavior of low-density high-strength FeeMneAleC steel are not thorough enough. In this paper, the microstructure evolution law and DRX behavior of the steel were studied using a thermal simulation compression experiment and metallographic observation. The flow stress curve characteristics of the steel were analyzed through the experimental data, and the dynamic recrystallization activation energy and Z parameters were calculated. The critical strain conditions for DRX were determined based on the Cingara-McQueen equation [10]. Functional relationships between rheological stress curve characteristic values (critical strain/stress, peak strain/ stress and steady-state strain/stress) and the dimensionless parameter Zener-Hollomon [11] were established. A dynamic recrystallization state diagram was drawn and a dynamic recrystallization average grain size prediction model was constructed. The research results provide theoretical support for the determination of the hot forging processes parameters as well as the numerical simulation of the hot forming of lowdensity high-strength Fe-Mn-Al-C steel

records.text: 2. Materials and methods
records.section: 2. Materials and methods

records.text: The material used in the experiment is FeeMneAleC steel and its main chemical composition (mass fraction, %) is: 1.46 C, 25.14 Mn, 10 Al, 0.053 Nb and the rest is Fe. The corresponding initial microstructure is shown in Fig. 1. The forging billet was processed into a cylindrical sample of F 8 mm 12 mm, and the perpendicularity of both ends of the samples was ensured. The isothermal constant strain rate compression experiments were carried out with the Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator. The experimental temperatures were 900, 950, 1000, 1050, 1100 and $1 1 5 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } ,$ , and the strain rates were 0.01, 0.1, 1 and $1 0 \ { \mathsf { s } } ^ { - 1 }$ , respectively. The maximum compression was 60% (corresponding to the maximum true strain 0.92). The mica foils with high-temperature lubricants were affixed to the two end faces of the sample to reduce the friction and the non-uniformity of deformation. The sample was heated to 1200 -C at a rate of ${ 1 0 ~ ^ { \circ } } \mathrm { C } / { \mathsf { s } }$ , then homogenized by holding for 120 s, and finally cooled to the set T at a rate of $5 ~ ^ { \circ } \subset / \mathsf { s } .$ . The sample was for 15 s at the set T before compression, so the temperature difference between the inside and outside of the sample was the same. After compression, the sample was sprayed with water to cool the steel down. Figure 2 shows the experimental process. The compressed sample was split in half along the axial axis, and after sample preparation, grinding, polishing and etching, the microstructure images were collected using a LEXT OLS4000 laser confocal microscope. The etching solution was: 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction). Through the Gleeble-3500 thermomechanical simulator, the isothermal constant strain rate thermal compression experiments of the same FeeMneAleC steel batch with the same composition can be confirmed under the same experimental conditions in order to check the reproducibility of the proposed system.

This leads to the work hardening effect being less than the softening effect of the material, showing that the rheological stress decreases with the decrease of <sup>ε</sup>\_. In addition, peak stress is an important basis for estimating maximum deformation load, die selection and equipment checking in actual production. Fig. 3 (c) and (d) are 3D peak stress maps of $\mathrm { F e { \mathrm { - } } M n { \mathrm { - } } A l { \mathrm { - } } C }$ steel under different T and <sup>ε</sup>\_. Fig. 3 (c) and (d) show that the peak stress of this steel is sensitive to <sup>ε</sup>\_ and T during hot deformation. At the low <sup>ε</sup>\_ (0.01 $\mathsf { \pmb { s } } ^ { - 1 } )$ , the peak stress decreased from 305.4 MPa at $9 0 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ to 53.8 MPa at $1 1 5 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } ,$ a reduction of 82%. When the <sup>ε</sup>\_ is high (10 $\mathsf { s } ^ { - 1 } ) _ { : }$ , the peak stress decreases by 73% within the same temperature range, indicating that <sup>ε</sup>\_ has a greater influence on the peak stress. The main reason is that the deformation time of the material is shortened with the increase of <sup>ε</sup>\_, the dislocation propagation rate is reduced, the DRV and DRX are insufficient, the softening effect is weak and the effect of work hardening is intensified, so the peak stress increases [12,13]. The same calculation can be obtained, in the case of a constant <sup>ε</sup>\_, the higher the T, the lower the peak stress, indicating that the peak stress is more sensitive to T. This is because the higher the T, the higher the thermal activation energy of the material, the faster the grain boundary mobility, the better the recrystallization and the lower the slip resistance, the stronger the softening effect and the lower the peak stress $[ 1 4 , 1 5 ]$ In summary, the steel can reduce the peak stress by reducing <sup>ε</sup>\_ or increasing T during hot deformation. The above experimental phenomena have reproducibility.

Zener and Hollomon [11] studied the constitutive relationship of steel and found that rheological stress depends on temperature and strain rate. records.text: The temperature compensated strain rate function (Z parameter formula (3)) has been applied in many studies. Singh et al. [18] studied the dynamic recrystallization of a high Nb-containing cast -TiAl based Tie45Ale8Nbe2Cr-0.2B alloy during hot compressive deformation and analyzed the Zener-Hollomon parameter modulated recrystallization mechanisms. Wang et al. [19] conducted the constitutive analysis of as-cast 40CrNiMo alloy steel through isothermal compression experiments and established the Arrhenius-type constitutive equation with the Zener-Hollomon parameter, having excellent accuracy. Detrois et al. [20] studied the hot deformation behavior of a Ni-based superalloy and simulated the flow stress from the experimental data using the Zener-Hollomon parameter.

records.text: 3.4. Microstructure evolution
records.section: 3.4. Microstructure evolution

records.text: During hot deformation, the microstructure of DRX directly affects the grain size of the forgings and then affects the mechanical properties of the materials. Due to the friction between the contact surface and the pressure head during compression, the stress in the material is unevenly distributed, leading to different deformation zones in the section parallel to the loading direction of the compression sample, as shown in Fig. 8. Among them, 1 is a difficult deformation zone, 2 is a small deformation zone and 3 is a large deformation zone. To comprehensively analyze the evolution law of microstructure of FeeMneAleC steel during hot deformation, the microstructure of three deformation zones in Fig. 8 was observed. The results are shown in Fig. 9 (1, 2 and 3 in Fig. 9 represent the corresponding microstructure of the zone of difficult deformation, the zone of small deformation and the zone of large deformation, respectively).

This may be because the dislocation motion is a hot activation process. The increase of T will increase the oscillation frequency of the atoms, promote the diffusion of atoms, the grain boundary migration and the dislocation motion, and then effectively induce the occurrence of DRX and make it fully performed [24,25]. Figure 10 shows the dynamic recrystallization average grain size of the steel under different T and <sup>ε</sup>\_ when the hot compression reaches 60%. The microstructure of the measured grain size is taken from the core of the compressed sample, which is the large deformation zone. Figure 10 shows that the DRX grain size of the steel after hot deformation increases with the decrease of <sup>ε</sup>\_ or the increase of T. Among them, when the T is $1 1 5 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ and the <sup>ε</sup>\_ is $0 . 0 1 { \mathsf { s } } ^ { - 1 }$ , the grain size exceeds $7 0 \ \mu \mathrm { m } ,$ and the structure is coarse grain, indicating that the recrystallized grains under this condition have grown rapidly. records.text: In conclusion, fine dynamic recrystallization grains tend to occur at low T and high <sup>ε</sup>\_ regions, but are not sufficient. The dynamic recrystallization average grain size obtained at high T and low <sup>ε</sup>\_ is large, which does not meet the fine grain size requirements. Therefore, combined with the observation of the microstructure and the variation of the dynamic recrystallization average grain size, sufficient dynamic recrystallization can be obtained by hot working within the range of $9 5 0 - 1 0 0 0 \ ^ { \circ } { \bf C } / 0 . 0 1 - 0 . 1 \ { \bf s } ^ { - 1 } \ { \mathrm { a n d } } \ 1 0 5 0 - 1 1 0 0 \ ^ { \circ } { \bf C } / 1 - 1 0 \ { \bf s } ^ { - 1 }$ , and the microstructure of the grain is relatively fine and uniform. The above experimental phenomena have reproducibility.

The correlation coefficient (R) was usually used to show the linear relations between the predicted and the experimental data. To evaluate the selected model, the average relative error (MRE) was considered an unbiased statistic for confirming the credibility of the model.
records.section: 3.5. Dynamic recrystallization average grain size prediction model

records.text: During the dynamic recrystallization of the material, the grain size constantly changes under the driving force. On the one hand, the grain growth is promoted under the action of temperature and plastic strain and the driving force has a positive effect on the grain size. On the other hand, dynamic recrystallization refines the microstructure inside the material and the driving force is a counter-driving force, which inhibits the grain growth [27e29]. This may cause errors in the dynamic recrystallization average grain size prediction model. In addition, there were some statistical errors. The results are shown in Fig. 11, R is 0.996 and MRE for all samples is only 4.53%, indicating a high degree of coincidence. Figure 11 (c) shows that the absolute error between the predicted value of the grain size and the experimental value is mostly within 3 m, which further shows that the model can accurately predict the dynamic recrystallization average grain size of low-density high-strength steel. It provides a reliable theoretical basis for the prediction of the dynamic recrystallized grain size of the steel after hot forging.

records.text: 4. Conclusion and prospect
records.section: 4. Conclusion and prospect

records.text: 4.1. Conclusion
records.section: 4.1. Conclusion

records.text: (1) FeeMneAleC steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain rate-sensitive material, and its rheological stress increases with the increase of $\dot { \varepsilon } \_ \mathrm { o r }$ the decrease of T. During hot deformation, the peak stress of the steel can be reduced by decreasing <sup>ε</sup>\_ or increasing T.
records.section: 4.1. Conclusion

records.text: (2) Based on the Arrhenius hyperbolic sine function equation, the dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the steel was calculated as 669.844 kJ $\mathrm { m o l } ^ { - 1 }$ . Through the introduction of the dimensionless parameter Zener-Hollomon, the $\varepsilon _ { \mathrm { c } } / \sigma _ { \mathrm { c } } , \varepsilon _ { \mathrm { p } } / \sigma _ { \mathrm { p } }$ and $\varepsilon _ { s } / \sigma _ { s }$ models of dynamic recrystallization were established, and the state diagram of DRX was drawn. The results show that with the increase of the Z parameter, the initiation and completion of the dynamic recrystallization behavior of the steel becomes more difficult.
records.section: 4.1. Conclusion

records.text: (3) The low T and high <sup>ε</sup>\_ are advantageous to obtain fine dynamic recrystallization grains, but they are not sufficient. With the decrease of <sup>ε</sup>\_ and the increase of T, full dynamic recrystallization of the material can be effectively induced and grain growth can also be caused. It is considered by comprehensive analysis that the fine and uniform grain structure can be obtained by hot working in the range of $9 5 0 - 1 0 0 0 \mathrm { ~  ~ { ~ \circ ~ } ~ } _ { \mathrm { C } / 0 . 0 1 - 0 . 1 } \mathrm { ~  ~ { ~ \mathbf ~ { ~ s } ^ { - 1 } } ~ }$ and 1050e1100 -C/1e10 s<sup>1</sup>.
records.section: 4.1. Conclusion

records.text: (4) The prediction model of dynamic recrystallization average grain size is drex 807743:63<sup>ε</sup>\_<sup>0:1903</sup> exp 120648:47 =RT 4:338, and the deviation is generally lower than $3 \mu \mathrm { m }$ , and MRE for all samples is only 4.53%, which indicates that the model can be used to predict the grain size of low-density high-strength steel during hot deformation.
records.section: 4.1. Conclusion

records.text: 4.2. Prospect
records.section: 4.2. Prospect

records.text: When setting the experimental conditions, we considered different parameters and obtained the best value of each parameter. Using multivariate research (experimental design and chemometrics), optimizing of two or more parameters is easier, more statistically correct and functional. At present, this multivariate method (experimental design) has been used in other studies (such as energy, environment and sensors). Hendriksen et al. [30] expanded the application of Noise2- Inverse in space, time and spectrum-like domains based on convolutional neural networks. The results on real-world datasets establish that Noise2Inverse can accurately denoise enabling a substantial reduction in the acquisition time while maintaining image quality. Galliano et al. [31] used the experimental design method to accurately study the effects of ${ \mathsf { C o } } ^ { 2 + }$ concentration, ${ \mathsf { C o } } ^ { 2 + } / { \mathsf { C o } } ^ { 3 - }$ <sup>þ</sup> ratio and xanthan gum dosage on the overall photovoltaic parameters of laboratory-scale solar cells at a multivariate level. Miccoli et al. [32] presented an efficient multisensor based on a single zinc oxide microwire/gold junction. The device can detect in real time three different stimuli, UV-VIS light, temperature and pH variations. It shows great potential for use in the field of biosensors. Yun et al. [33] used headspace vaporized GC/MS (HS-GC/MS) to analyze black tea samples collected from 10 geographic origins. The findings support the use of HS-GC/MS combined with chemometrics as a tool to identify the origin of black tea. Galliano et al. [34] have adopted an experimental strategy of multivariate chemometric approach to study the main factors influencing dye-sensitized solar cells efficiency and stability and obtained an optimized system which can improve their efficiency. Bella et al. [35] proposed the replacement of the liquid electrolyte with quasi-linear polymer electrolyte membranes, with the aim of increasing the durability of the device. The experimental conditions are investigated and optimized by means of a multivariate chemometric approach, and the characterization of the materials and devices was presented.
records.section: 4.2. Prospect

records.text: In conclusion, we will carry out the multivariate study in future work in order to take into account all the relevant variables and their interactions, finding the best experimental conditions for the proper functioning of their materials/devices/reactors.
records.section: 4.2. Prospect
